acceptanceCriteria: When the dispatcher observes its launched worker process has exited and the attempt is still RUNNING, it retries `release --reason HANDOFF` itself with a bounded backoff.

Once the lease has expired and the release has not succeeded, the dispatcher reaps the attempt and quarantines the pool member exactly as reap does today; an attempt already FAILED/FENCED is treated as resolved, not as needs-owner.
`needs-owner` is reported only when both the release and the reap fail; a dispatcher config switch (default on) disables the automatic path.
Maintained tests cover worker-exit with live lease (release), with expired lease (reap), with an already fenced attempt (no needs-owner), and with the switch off.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 from GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#622 (orchestrator triage; reporter observations on main-2fff511, not reproduced yet).

When a dispatcher-launched worker exits and its attempt is still RUNNING, the dispatcher only reports `needs-owner` and leaves the attempt RUNNING and the pool member ALLOCATED until a human acts. Six occurrences in about 24 h on program flowproof (main-2fff511); the reporter runs an external steward.

Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-06-v1-0851-worker-exit-recovery.md at that commit (the digest is that file's sha256), which records the change, the maintained tests the acceptance criteria name, the independent Codex review and its repairs. The batch head passed the doc gates, go vet, the full suites of the touched packages on darwin and every hosted CI check (go-product shards, doc-gates, go-interop). NOT_RUN: make gate, live multi-agent/dispatcher qualification and non-darwin execution where that entry says so.

title: corvint-tasks dispatch: release (HANDOFF, bounded retry) or reap a worker's RUNNING attempt when the launched worker exits, before reporting needs-owner (issue #622)
